*'This is it,'* she thought, *'my first encounter with a human... I must be cautious, but oh, how exhilarating!'*

 
Rounding the corner of the tent, Olivette was not prepared for the abruptness of the encounter. The flap of the tent gaped open like a yawning mouth, and there, within, was a figure, a human figure. entries.name: Pocket Lamia Appearance
entries.content: Pocket Lamia range in size, but rarely grow larger than a house cat, and often end up about the size of a gopher snake—though some can be as small as a garter snake. From the waist up, Pocket Lamia have the form of miniature humans, and from the waist down they have the scaled sinuous body of a snake. Pocket Lamia come in infinite combinations of skin, hair and eye color, their appearance as varied as any other race. Their scaled lower bodies demonstrate a bright range of hues and patterns. Pocket Lamia are cold-blooded and enjoy curling up around their owner's fingers and limbs for warmth.

entries.name: Pocket Lamia - SFW
entries.content: Pocket Lamia, also called Companion Lamia, are a chimeric species that evolved alongside humans. Like dogs and cats, Lamia have been a part of human culture for generations, providing both companionship and assistance with many tasks. Pocket Lamia are a cultural staple of many human societies, while somewhat rare, most modern people would know of them.

Pocket Lamia with female genitalia can safely take the penis of an adult human inside them. entries.name: Pocket Lamia Ancestry
entries.content: Pocket Lamia as a species have high mutability, this has allowed them to adapt strongly to evolving alongside humans, roughly matching their intelligence, speech, and day/night cycle. Instead of being made magically, Pocket Lamia evolved from an ancient unknown ancestor.

entries.name: Pocket Lamia Diet
entries.content:
Like their human counterparts, Pocket Lamia have evolved to be omnivorous, able to eat most things humans can. Despite this, many Pocket Lamia still retain their hunting instinct and enjoy catching and eating life prey. Their usual quarry would be bugs and small rats.
Peculiarly, most Pocket Lamia have an intense love of blackberries.

Owing to their small size and fragile bodies most cultures require Pocket Lamia to have an owner, parent, or guardian. Having long served as primarily companions in their shared cultures, most Pocket Lamia desire a human to bond with, either through ownership, genuine interest, or in rare circumstances, romantic entanglement.
